title: Job-board refresh sweep isolation
notes: In-process, fetch mocked (design §4.7 'Job refresh sweep'). Drives the REAL careeronestop/talroo/adzuna/jsearch/usajobs adapters (src/lib/job-board/adapters/*.ts) concurrently via Promise.allSettled — the same shape runScrapeForConfig uses — with jsearch configured to hang and usajobs to 500. Both go through fetchJson's VQ-R-019 hardening, which never throws on either failure and returns [] instead, so 'adapters_completed_despite_failure' counts adapters that actually delivered postings (careeronestop, talroo, adzuna = 3 = adapter count − 2), not merely settled-without-rejecting (which would always read 5/5 and hide a regression). sweep_ms measured 203ms in a --self-test run on this container (up to ~18 sequential mocked fetchJson calls across careeronestop's WV pass + per-title passes and talroo's per-title loop, plus the ~150ms fastTimeoutMs wait for jsearch's hang); the 1000ms floor is about 5x that with a 200ms tolerance, deliberately generous because the property under test is 'does not serialize behind the hang' rather than a tight timing target — a regression that turns the sweep sequential (18 real awaits instead of one Promise.allSettled) or that stops honoring the per-adapter timeout would blow well past 1000ms, while ordinary CI jitter should not. The suite also races the whole sweep against a 5s deadline (fixture raceDeadlineMs) so a genuine regression (the hang never isolated) throws a clear error instead of hanging the CI job. AbortSignal.timeout is monkey-patched to fire in ~150ms rather than waiting out the real 30_000ms constant — same technique as jsearch.test.ts/adzuna.test.ts — so this measures the TIMEOUT MECHANISM, not the literal constant.
